newsitem.title: USA: AMD to cut K6 prices to keep pace with Intel.
newsitem.headline: AMD to cut K6 prices to keep pace with Intel.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc will cut prices of its K6 computer chip when Intel Corp lowers prices on its chips later this summer, a spokesman said Wednesday.

"We will stay competitive from a price point of view with Intel," said Scott Allen, an AMD spokesman. "We've been defining 'competitive' as 25 percent less than the price of competing products from Intel."
AMD's K6 works just like top-of-the-line microprocessors in Intel's Pentium chips, the components that control the basic functions of about 80 percent of the world's personal computers.

Each quarter, Intel cuts the prices of Pentiums to keep up sales momentum. Analysts expect Intel to cut its prices more deeply than usual in August in the face of competition from AMD and Cyrix Corp, another Intel-compatible chipmaker.
Allen would not say how much AMD planned to cut its prices. He said AMD would announce its price cuts on the heels of any Intel announcements, without being more specific.
Currently, AMD sells its K6 chips at three speeds for prices ranging between $244 to $469 in batches of 1,000.
